challenges.title: Not a secret code
challenges.body:
A developer said this config value was "encrypted". Was it?
```
YWF5YXR7YmFzZTY0X2lzX25vdF9lbmNyeXB0aW9ufQ==
```
challenges.hint: Ends in == and uses only letters, digits, + and /. That shape has a name.
challenges.solve: CyberChef: From Base64.

challenges.title: Layers
challenges.body:
Malware often hides a string under several encodings. Peel them off one at a time.
```
626d3573626d643759334a796556397961584a6c62463935626d78795a58303d
```
challenges.hint: Only 0-9 and a-f at first. After that, look at what each step gives you. The last layer shifts every letter by 13.
challenges.solve: From Hex, then From Base64, then ROT13.

challenges.title: One-byte XOR
challenges.body:
This beacon string was XORed with a single secret byte (hex):
```
3b3b233b2e212235280538282f2e3f053c3528393f052d33342927
```
A one-byte key has only 256 possibilities.
challenges.hint: CyberChef: From Hex, then XOR Brute Force. Search the results for aayat.
challenges.solve: From Hex, then XOR with key 5A (or XOR Brute Force and filter on 'aayat').

challenges.title: Old-school cipher
challenges.body:
An intercepted note, encrypted with the Vigenère cipher:
```
shgee{nwfa_qlwllz_qzuw_apey_fawpicv}
```
The key is the six-letter word for what a knight raises to block a blow.
challenges.hint: CyberChef has Vigenère Decode. The key is SHIELD.
challenges.solve: Vigenère Decode with key SHIELD.

challenges.title: Crack the leaked hash
challenges.body:
A leaked database row stores this unsalted SHA-256 password hash:
```
a9c43be948c5cabd56ef2bacffb77cdaa5eec49dd5eb0cc4129cf3eda5f0e74c
```
Try each word from this common-password list:
```
password
sunshine
monkey
football
dragon
letmein
princess
qwerty
shadow
master
```
The flag is aayat{the_password}.
challenges.hint: Hash each word with SHA2 (256) in CyberChef, or loop over the list with sha256sum in the Linux lab.
challenges.solve: sha256('dragon') matches. Unsalted, fast hashes of common words fall to a wordlist in seconds.

challenges.title: Read the token
challenges.body:
This login token came back from a web app. Anyone holding it can read it. Can you?
```
eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiIxMDQyIiwibmFtZSI6InByaXlhIiwicm9sZSI6InN0dWRlbnQiLCJub3RlIjoiYWF5YXR7and0c19hcmVfc2lnbmVkX25vdF9zZWNyZXR9In0.k3Vn1u0dWQ2vQ6hT9cX8xS1rR0mY7pZ4aB2cD5eF6gH
```
challenges.hint: Three parts separated by dots. CyberChef: JWT Decode.
challenges.solve: JWT Decode (or From Base64 on the middle part). A signature stops changes, but it doesn't hide the payload.

challenges.title: Café Wi-Fi capture
challenges.body:
On open café Wi-Fi you captured this plain-HTTP request:
```
GET /portal HTTP/1.1
Host: intranet.example.com
Authorization: Basic cHJpeWE6YWF5YXR7aHR0cF9iYXNpY19pc19qdXN0X2Jhc2U2NH0=
User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0
```
The flag is the password.
challenges.hint: The Basic scheme is just base64 of user:password.
challenges.solve: Base64-decode the header: priya:aayat{...}. Without HTTPS, anyone on the network can read it.

challenges.solve: 203.0.113.66 hits 18 different destination ports in 18 seconds. 192.0.2.44 only retries port 22, which is brute force.

challenges.title: Where does this link really go?
challenges.body:
A text message says your bank account is locked and links to:
```
https://secure.mybank.com.account-verify.xyz/login?session=8812
```
Which registered domain will your browser actually contact? Flag: aayat{domain}
challenges.hint: Read the hostname right to left. The registered domain is the part just before the top-level domain.
challenges.solve: The hostname ends in account-verify.xyz. Everything before that is a subdomain the attacker controls.

challenges.title: Read the email headers
challenges.body:
The display name says PayPal. The headers tell a different story:
```
From: "PayPal Service" <service@paypal.com>
Reply-To: billing@paypa1-support.top
Return-Path: <bounce@paypa1-support.top>
Received: from mail.paypa1-support.top (45.13.0.9)
Authentication-Results: spf=fail smtp.mailfrom=paypa1-support.top; dkim=none
Subject: Your account has been limited
```
Which domain really sent it? Flag: aayat{domain}
challenges.hint: Look at Return-Path and the SPF result, not the From line.
challenges.solve: Return-Path and Received both show paypa1-support.top (a digit 1, not an l), and SPF fails for it.

challenges.title: A cloned badge
challenges.body:
Badge reader log for one building. One badge is in two places at once, so somebody cloned it.
```
07:58:02 B-1180 Main lobby
07:59:40 B-4471 Main lobby
08:01:13 B-2093 Main lobby
08:03:55 B-1180 Lab 2
08:04:10 B-4471 Server room
08:04:12 B-4471 Loading dock
08:06:31 B-2093 Office 3
08:09:02 B-3307 Main lobby
08:12:45 B-3307 Office 1
```
Flag: aayat{badge id}
challenges.hint: The server room and the loading dock are at opposite ends of the building.
challenges.solve: B-4471 swipes the server room and the loading dock two seconds apart. That's impossible for one person, so the badge was cloned.

challenges.title: Linux lab: crack it
challenges.body: Open the Linux lab, press Start and then Create the lab files. ~/lab/leaked_hash.txt is a SHA-256 of a password from ~/lab/wordlist.txt. The flag is aayat{password}.
challenges.hint: Lab card 4 has a loop that hashes every word.
challenges.solve: for w in $(cat wordlist.txt); do ... sha256sum ... done finds letmein.

challenges.title: Linux lab: who got in with a key?
challenges.body: In the Linux lab, ~/lab/auth.log records SSH logins. One account signed in with a public key instead of a password. The flag is aayat{username}.
challenges.hint: grep Accepted auth.log
challenges.solve: grep Accepted auth.log shows 'Accepted publickey for deploy'.

challenges.title: SQL injection: walk in as admin
challenges.body: Log in to the staff portal as admin without knowing the password. Open the SQL injection lab; the flag appears when you succeed.
challenges.hint: Close the quote, add a condition that is always true, then comment out the rest.
challenges.solve: Username: admin' -- (or ' OR 1=1 --). The password check is commented out.

challenges.title: SQL injection: hidden stock
challenges.body: The product search only shows products where hidden = 0. Make it list the hidden ones too. Open the SQL injection lab; the flag appears when you succeed.
challenges.hint: Your text lands inside LIKE '%...%'. Close it, then OR in a condition about hidden.
challenges.solve: Search: %' OR hidden = 1 --

challenges.title: SQL injection: UNION heist
challenges.body: There is a table called secrets. Pull its contents into the product search results. Open the SQL injection lab; the flag appears when you succeed.
challenges.hint: UNION SELECT needs the same number of columns as the original query: two.
challenges.solve: Search: ' UNION SELECT note, 0 FROM secrets --

challenges.title: SQL injection: fix it
challenges.body: Rewrite the login query with ? placeholders so all the attacks fail and real logins still work. Open the SQL injection lab; the flag appears when you succeed.
challenges.hint: Keep the query, but replace each quoted value with a bare ?.
challenges.solve: SELECT id, username, role FROM users WHERE username = ? AND password = ?

challenges.title: Shop: leaky errors
challenges.body: Make the shop show you a raw database error. Open the vulnerable shop; the flag appears when you succeed.
challenges.hint: What does a search for a single quote do?
challenges.solve: Search for ' and the API returns the SQL error with the full query.

challenges.title: Shop: log in as the admin
challenges.body: Log in as admin@nimbu.shop without the password. Open the vulnerable shop; the flag appears when you succeed.
challenges.hint: The email field goes straight into SQL.
challenges.solve: Email: admin@nimbu.shop' -- with any password.

challenges.title: Shop: the page nobody links to
challenges.body: Find and open the shop's administration page. Open the vulnerable shop; the flag appears when you succeed.
challenges.hint: Look through the shop's JavaScript in the Sources tab for route names. You'll need an admin session.
challenges.solve: Sources lists #/administration. Open it while logged in as admin.

challenges.title: Shop: other people's orders
challenges.body: Read an order that belongs to somebody else. Open the vulnerable shop; the flag appears when you succeed.
challenges.hint: Open one of your orders and watch the API call in the Network tab. What if you change the number?
challenges.solve: GET /api/orders/1 works for any logged-in user. The server never checks the owner.

challenges.title: Shop: forgotten backup
challenges.body: Find a backup file the developers forgot to remove. Open the vulnerable shop; the flag appears when you succeed.
challenges.hint: Every site has a file that tells search engines where not to look.
challenges.solve: /robots.txt disallows /ftp; /ftp lists backup-2026.bak, and the flag is inside it.

challenges.title: Shop: stored XSS
challenges.body: Post a product review that makes the page pop up an alert box for everyone who views it. Open the vulnerable shop; the flag appears when you succeed.
challenges.hint: Reviews are inserted as HTML. A
challenges.solve: Review text:

challenges.title: Shop: they pay you
challenges.body: Check out with a basket total below zero. Open the vulnerable shop; the flag appears when you succeed.
challenges.hint: The page won't let you type a negative quantity, but the API is a different story. Use Edit and resend.
challenges.solve: Resend POST /api/basket with "qty": -10, then check out.

challenges.title: Shop: zero stars
challenges.body: Send feedback with a rating of 0. The form only lets you choose 1 to 5. Open the vulnerable shop; the flag appears when you succeed.
challenges.hint: The limit only exists in the browser. Resend the request with your own value.
challenges.solve: Resend POST /api/feedback with "rating": 0.

challenges.title: Shop: reset Jim's password
challenges.body: Reset the password for jim@nimbu.shop using his security question. Open the vulnerable shop; the flag appears when you succeed.
challenges.hint: His question asks for his pet's name. Jim talks a lot in product reviews.
challenges.solve: Jim's review of the cat-ear headset mentions his dog Bruno. Answer: Bruno.

challenges.title: Shop: forge a token
challenges.body: Without the admin password, make the API accept you as admin by editing your token. Open the vulnerable shop; the flag appears when you succeed.
challenges.hint: Decode your token in the Storage tab. What happens if alg says none and you drop the signature?
challenges.solve: Set header {"alg":"none"}, payload role admin, keep the trailing dot with no signature, save it and open the admin page.

challenges.title: The invoice that wasn't
challenges.body: Work the Kestrel Logistics ransomware runbook. The loader left a settings file behind, and its campaign value is encoded. Decode it.
challenges.hint: Step 7 of the runbook. The value after campaign= is base64: try base64 -d.
challenges.solve: grep '^campaign=' suspect/upd.cfg | cut -d= -f2- | base64 -d

challenges.title: The night shift download
challenges.body: Work the Halcyon insider runbook. Something plugged into eng-ws57 at 02:05 had a very unusual name.
challenges.hint: Read usb.log, or build the timeline in step 7.
challenges.solve: The USB volume label in usb.log.

challenges.title: Follow the beacon home
challenges.body: Work the NimbuMart web server runbook. The attacker kept notes on their own staging server. What tag did they sign with?
challenges.hint: Step 7: nmap the attacker's address, then curl the web server you find on it.
challenges.solve: curl -s http://203.0.113.7:8080/notes.txt

challenges.title: The key in the commit
challenges.body: Work the Paperplane cloud key runbook. The secret was deleted from the repo the next day. Deleted is not the same as gone.
challenges.hint: Step 3: read the whole Git history, including what the delete commit removed.
challenges.solve: The comment line in config/staging.env in repo_history.txt.

challenges.title: Exam day outage
challenges.body: Work the Northfield exam outage runbook. The HTTP flood signs every request with the same user agent. Read it closely.
challenges.hint: Step 4: count the user agents in access.log, or read the http.user_agent field in the capture.
challenges.solve: The user agent of the GET /login?ts= flood.

challenges.title: The table nobody mentioned
challenges.body: The Northwind staff portal has a table it never shows. Find it and read it.
challenges.hint: sqlite_master lists every table. Use UNION in the product search.
challenges.solve: ' UNION SELECT name, 1 FROM sqlite_master -- then ' UNION SELECT note, 1 FROM hr_bonus_2026 --

challenges.title: Yes or no
challenges.body: The username checker only answers taken or free. That is enough to read admin's PIN.
challenges.hint: admin' AND substr(pin,1,1)='4' -- is taken only when the guess is right.
challenges.solve: Boolean blind SQL injection on the username checker, one digit at a time.

challenges.title: Coupon twice
challenges.body: WELCOME10 is meant to work once per customer.
challenges.hint: The shop remembers the code exactly as typed, but accepts it in any case.
challenges.solve: Apply WELCOME10, then welcome10.

challenges.title: Open redirect
challenges.body: Make a nimbu.shop link that sends people anywhere you like.
challenges.hint: Look for /go?to= in Sources.
challenges.solve: /go?to=https://example.com

challenges.title: Not a picture
challenges.body: Upload a profile picture that runs JavaScript.
challenges.hint: The check only looks for .png somewhere in the name.
challenges.solve: Upload me.png.html containing , then open /uploads/me.png.html.

challenges.title: Look-alike letters
challenges.body:
This sign-in link looks right, but one letter is not what it seems:
```
https://аpple-id.example/verify
```
Which alphabet does the first letter of the domain come from? The flag is aayat{ALPHABET_a} in lowercase, for example aayat{greek_a}.
challenges.hint: Paste it into CyberChef and use To Hex. A normal a is 61. Look up the bytes you get.
challenges.solve: To Hex shows d0 b0: Cyrillic small letter a (U+0430).

challenges.title: Where does the short link go?
challenges.body:
A text message said your parcel is stuck and gave a short link. Someone saved what the link did, but encoded it:
```

```
challenges.hint: From Base64 in CyberChef. Follow each hop to the last page.
challenges.solve: From Base64; the last line holds the flag.

challenges.title: Cloned badge
challenges.hint: From Hex in CyberChef.
challenges.solve: From Hex.

challenges.title: Serial number
challenges.body: In the Halcyon insider runbook, what was the serial number of the USB drive? The flag is aayat{SERIAL}.
challenges.hint: usb.log, the device connected line.
challenges.solve: grep serial usb.log

challenges.title: The port nobody opened
challenges.body: In the hacked web shop runbook, a full port scan of web01 finds one port that shouldn't be there. The flag is aayat{PORT}.

challenges.title: Name before the download
challenges.body: In the Kestrel ransomware runbook, which domain did hr-pc07 look up just before it downloaded the second stage? The flag is aayat{DOMAIN}.
challenges.hint: tshark -r capture.pcap -Y dns
challenges.solve: tshark -r capture.pcap -Y dns -T fields -e ip.src -e dns.qry.name

challenges.title: Three digits
challenges.body: A script must be readable, writable and runnable by its owner, readable and runnable by its group, and nothing at all for anyone else. Which chmod number? The flag is aayat{NUMBER}.
challenges.hint: r=4, w=2, x=1. Add them for owner, group, others. Try it with chmod and ls -l in the Linux lab.

challenges.title: Weak hash, short list
challenges.body:
A password database leaked this MD5 hash:
```
d8578edf8458ce06fbc5bb76a58c5ca4
```
The password is in ~/lab/wordlist.txt in the Linux lab. The flag is aayat{PASSWORD}.
challenges.hint: Press Create the lab files, then loop over the wordlist with md5sum, like step 4 does with sha256sum.
challenges.solve: for w in $(cat wordlist.txt); do echo -n $w | md5sum | grep -q d8578edf8458ce06fbc5bb76a58c5ca4 && echo $w; done

A developer left a debugging note inside this login token. Tokens are signed, not secret.

challenges.solve: JWT Decode, read the debug claim.

challenges.title: The backdoor account
challenges.body: In the Paperplane cloud key runbook, what is the name of the user the attacker created? The flag is aayat{USERNAME}.
